anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 76 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: καθ' ὁμοιότητα καὶ εἰκόνα Θεοῦ together with rule over all on the earth recalls LXX Genesis 1:26 κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν, καὶ ἀρχέτωσαν ... πάσης τῆς γῆς; Cyril reverses the order and uses ὁμοιότης for ὁμοίωσις.

choices.why: Idiom 'nothing prevents'; λυπέω here does not mean 'grieve'.
An honorific form of address to a bishop; a literal 'your God-fearingness' would read as a calque.
Cyril's own term for the consecrated Eucharist; kept so the reader meets his word, with the meaning given in a note.

choices.english: They are mad to say this.
choices.why: μαίνομαι is strong ('rave, be mad'); the English keeps the force.
rejected: They are mistaken in saying this.

edition.locus: Ep remainder, close ('He holds rule over all' to 'They are mad to say this')

pass_a_gloss: [having been allotted to rule] all the things on the earth according to likeness (ὁμοιότητα) and image (εἰκόνα) of God. Therefore according to being a rational animal (ζῷον λογικόν) and inasmuch as [he is] virtue-loving (φιλάρετον) and ruling (ἀρχικόν) of the things on earth, he is said to have been made in the image of God. But if they suppose the image to be spoken according to the shape (σχῆμα) of the body, nothing hinders (οὐδὲν λυπεῖ) also to say God to be same-formed (σύμμορφον) with the irrational (ἀλόγοις) of the animals. For we see that they too are of the same members (μορίων) as us, having feet and mouth and eyes and nostrils and tongue and the other of the members (μελῶν) of the body. Let your God-reverence (θεοσέβεια) then stop such people, or rather also rebuke (ἐπιτιμάτω) those accustomed to babble (φλυαρεῖν) these things. And I hear that they say the mystical blessing (μυστικὴν εὐλογίαν) is inactive (ἀπρακτεῖν) toward sanctification (ἁγιασμόν), if a remnant (λείψανον) of it should remain to another day. And they rave (μαίνονται) saying these things; for not [continues beyond this row: ἀλλοιοῦται Χριστός ...].
pass_b_english: He holds rule over all that is on the earth, after the likeness and image of God (Genesis 1:26).
So it is because he is a rational living being, a lover of virtue, and a ruler over the things of the earth that he is said to have been made in the image of God.
But if they think the image refers to the shape of the body, then nothing stops them from saying that God shares the form of the brute animals as well.
For we see that they too are made of the same parts as we are: they have feet and a mouth, eyes, nostrils and a tongue, and the other members of the body.
Let your Reverence, then, put a stop to such people, or rather, rebuke those who make a habit of babbling such things.
I hear, too, that they say the mystical blessing has no power to sanctify if any of it is left over until another day.
They are mad to say this.
source_text:
ἁπάντων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καθ' ὁμοιότητα καὶ εἰκόνα Θεοῦ. οὐκοῦν κατὰ τὸ εἶναι
ζῷον λογικὸν καὶ καθὸ φιλάρετον καὶ ἀρχικὸν τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἐν εἰκόνι Θεοῦ
πεποιῆσθαι λέγεται. εἰ δὲ νομίζουσι κατὰ τὸ τοῦ σώματος σχῆμα λέγεσθαι τὴν
εἰκόνα, οὐδὲν λυπεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἀλόγοις τῶν ζῴων σύμμορφον λέγειν εἶναι τὸν Θεόν.
ὁρῶμεν γὰρ, ὅτι καὶ αὐτὰ ἐκ τῶν αὐτῶν ἡμῖν εἰσι μορίων, πόδας ἔχοντα καὶ στόμα
καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ ῥῖνας καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ τὰ ἕτερα τῶν τοῦ σώματος μελῶν.
παυέτω τοίνυν ἡ σὴ θεοσέβεια τοὺς τοιούτους, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐπιτιμάτω τοῖς ταῦτα
φλυαρεῖν εἰωθόσιν.
Ἀκούω δὲ ὅτι φασὶν ἀπρακτεῖν εἰς ἁγιασμὸν τὴν μυστικὴν εὐλογίαν, εἰ
ἀπομείνοι λείψανον αὐτῆς εἰς ἑτέραν ἡμέραν. μαίνονται δὲ ταῦτα λέγοντες· οὐ γὰρ

review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row that held no translation; the English is new, translated from the locked PG 76 Greek in translations/ac_ep_rem_source.json.

The source section ends with οὐ γὰρ, the first words of the next sentence; the English stops at 'They are mad to say this.' The rest of the letter is in sources/ad_calosyrium_pg.txt but not yet in a locked section.
Genesis 1:26 checked against LXX (κατ' εἰκόνα ... καθ' ὁμοίωσιν, καὶ ἀρχέτωσαν ... πάσης τῆς γῆς).
Negations kept: 'nothing stops them', 'has no power to sanctify'.
